edges.mechanism: Garlic supplements reduced saquinavir AUC 51%, trough 49% and Cmax 54%, with incomplete recovery after a 10-day washout; ex vivo data implicate increased intestinal P-gp/MRP2 efflux.
edges.evidence: Open-label PK study in 10 healthy volunteers plus ex vivo mechanistic work and review; moderate certainty for PK effect

edges.mechanism: Possible reduced exposure via intestinal efflux/first-pass changes (often described as CYP3A4 induction, but probe phenotyping showed no CYP3A4 change); short-term garlic did not significantly alter single-dose ritonavir.
edges.evidence: Human PK studies (n=10 each), probe-phenotyping RCT, ex vivo data; low certainty outside saquinavir

edges.mechanism: Antiplatelet activity may add to anticoagulation; case reports of over-anticoagulation (warfarin, fluindione), but a crossover RCT found no change in warfarin PK/INR and AGE did not increase bleeding in 48 warfarin patients.
edges.evidence: Case reports, systematic reviews, crossover RCT (n=12), pilot RCT of AGE (n=48); low certainty

edges.mechanism: Additive effect on hemostasis; garlic among supplements most strongly associated with surgical bleeding.
edges.evidence: Narrative reviews and case reports; low certainty

edges.mechanism: AGE inhibits ADP-induced aggregation and garlic oil modestly reduces adrenaline-induced aggregation; additive with aspirin/P2Y12 inhibitors plausible, though dietary doses did not impair platelet function tests.
edges.evidence: Small human platelet trials and reviews; no clinical outcome study; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Bleeding risk (spinal epidural hematoma case); ASA/AANA advise stopping herbal products 1-2 weeks before elective surgery.
edges.evidence: Case report, perioperative reviews; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Qualitative platelet dysfunction reported with heavy garlic intake; additive to underlying hemostatic defects.
edges.evidence: Case report and review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Garlic extract lowered isoniazid Cmax ~65% and AUC ~55% in rabbits; rifampicin unaffected.
edges.evidence: Single animal PK study; no human data; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Garlic oil inhibited CYP2E1 by 22-39% and diallyl sulfide reduced chlorzoxazone hydroxylation in volunteers.
edges.evidence: Probe-drug phenotyping studies in healthy young and older adults; moderate certainty for the PK effect, clinical relevance uncertain

edges.mechanism: CYP3A substrate; garlic 600 mg twice daily did not significantly change clearance overall, but exposure rose markedly in CYP3A5*1A/*1A carriers (n=3).
edges.evidence: PK study in 10 patients with metastatic breast cancer; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Additive BP lowering (SBP about -4 to -9 mmHg in hypertensive adults).
edges.evidence: Multiple MAs of RCTs; moderate certainty for BP effect, no interaction trials

edges.mechanism: Small additive glucose lowering (FBG -2.76 mg/dL, HbA1c -0.53%); a chlorpropamide interaction is reported.
edges.evidence: GRADE MA of 27 RCTs; interaction review; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Duplicate garlic exposure: aged garlic extract also inhibits ADP-induced platelet aggregation and lowers SBP/LDL, so antiplatelet and BP effects are additive; treat combined use as a single garlic exposure for bleeding and perioperative purposes.
edges.evidence: AGE platelet trial, AGE dose-response MA, perioperative review; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Complementary lipid effects: garlic lowered LDL and fish oil lowered TG, and the combination offset the fish-oil LDL rise; both appear in reviews of supplements affecting hemostasis.
edges.evidence: Single 12-week RCT (n=50) plus review; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Both reviewed as supplements that may interfere with hemostasis; stacking is a theoretical additive bleeding risk.
edges.evidence: Narrative review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Both reviewed as supplements that may interfere with hemostasis; stacking is a theoretical additive bleeding risk.
edges.evidence: Narrative review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Turmeric associated with bleeding in anticoagulated patients; garlic associated with surgical bleeding; additive exposure inferred.
edges.evidence: Narrative review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: IgE-mediated allergy (alliin lyase major allergen, heat labile; powder retains raw-garlic proteins); urticaria, angioedema, anaphylaxis reported.
edges.evidence: Case reports and review; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Volatile organosulfur compounds cause chemical (mostly second-degree) burns on skin and mucosa.
edges.evidence: Systematic review of 39 cases

edges.mechanism: Garlic flavours breast milk and alters infant nursing behaviour.
edges.evidence: Controlled study in mother-infant dyads; low certainty

edges.mechanism: True pharmacological inhibition (ADP Km roughly doubled after AGE) may alter aggregometry; dietary raw garlic did not change PFA-100/Multiplate/TEG.
edges.evidence: Small human studies; low certainty
